6:This chapter defines the two testing primitives underlying the question-reduction step: the \emph{classical low individual degree game}, in its simultaneous form, and the \emph{Pauli basis test}, a nonlocal game built from the classical game together with the Magic Square game. We state the quantum soundness of the classical game (Theorem~\ref{lem:ld-soundness}, imported, with the facts required by the identification, which remain to be proved, recorded in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; see Remark~\ref{rem:ld-soundness-provider}), the rigidity of the Magic Square game (Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-rigidity}, imported), completeness of the Pauli basis test (Lemma~\ref{lem:pauli-completeness}), and the main soundness theorem for the Pauli basis test (Theorem~\ref{thm:pauli}), whose proof occupies Chapters~\ref{chap:qpbt-observables}--\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} and is completed in Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-extraction} only modulo the proof obligation documented in \cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}. The chapter closes with the qubit form of the soundness statement (Corollary~\ref{cor:pauli-binary}) and the canonical parameter choice with its soundness bound (Definition~\ref{def:introparams}, Lemma~\ref{lem:delta-bound}).
182:\section{The Magic Square game}
186:We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
188:\begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
190:	The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.
194:		\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} &= \{\mathsf{Constraint}_i : i = 1,2,\ldots,6\}\;,\\
198:	where $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ denotes the constraint of row $i$ (with variables $x_{3(i-1)+1}, x_{3(i-1)+2}, x_{3(i-1)+3}$), $\mathsf{Constraint}_4$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_5$ denote the constraints of the first two columns, and $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$ denotes the constraint of the third column (with variables $x_{i-3}, x_{i}, x_{i+3}$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$, $i \in \{4,5,6\}$).
200:	The question distribution is as follows: the verifier samples $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ uniformly from $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$, then samples $\mathsf{Variable}_j$ uniformly among the three variables appearing in the row or column of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; one player, chosen uniformly at random, receives $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and the other receives $\mathsf{Variable}_j$. Equivalently, the verifier samples a uniformly random edge of the bipartite \emph{type graph} $G^{\mathrm{ms}}$ on vertex sets $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$ and $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}$, whose edges are $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{3(i-1)+j}$ for $i,j \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{(i-3)+3(j-1)}$ for $i \in \{4,5,6\}$, $j \in \{1,2,3\}$ ($18$ edges in total, and no self-loops), and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other endpoint to the other player.
202:	The $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player answers with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$, where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; the $\mathsf{Variable}$ player answers with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$. The players win if and only if the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player's answer satisfies the equation associated with $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
205:The following theorem records the self-testing (rigidity) properties of the Magic Square game. It is used in the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test to enforce anticommutation relations between certain pairs of observables.

232:The converse construction shows that any pair of anticommuting binary observables yields a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game.

260:	so the bottom-right cell is Hermitian, and it squares to the identity; hence every cell is a genuine $\pm 1$-valued observable. The three observables in each row and each column commute pairwise --- for the third row and third column this again uses Equation~\eqref{eq:am-i-hermitian} --- so the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ measurements are well defined, and the strategy is symmetric, projective, and commuting. A two-outcome projective measurement is consistent on a state if and only if its observable $\mathcal O$ satisfies $\mathcal O \ot I \ket{\psi} = I \ot \mathcal O \ket{\psi}$; since $A$ and $B$ are consistent on $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot n}$ by hypothesis and $\sigma^X$, $\sigma^Z$ are consistent on $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$, each cell observable is a product of consistent, commuting factors and is therefore consistent on $\ket{\psi}$, and consistency of the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ measurements follows from the cellwise consistencies together with commutativity. Finally, the observables in each row and each of the first two columns multiply to $I$, while those of the third column multiply to $-I$; for the measurement $\{S_0, S_1\}$ obtained by measuring a $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ triple and outputting the sum of the three bits, the observable $S_0 - S_1$ equals the product of the three cell observables, hence $\pm I$, which forces the three answer bits to sum to $0$ (respectively, $1$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$) with certainty. Together with consistency this shows that every check of the Magic Square game is passed with probability $1$, so the strategy has value $1$.
267:The Pauli basis test is the quantum low individual degree test of Natarajan and Vidick, in the slightly modified form introduced by Natarajan and Wright~\cite{Natarajan2018NEEXP}. Informally, the test certifies that the players share the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot M}$, where $M = 2^m$. On a question of type $(\mathsf{Pauli}, W)$ with $W \in \{X,Z\}$, a player is expected to measure the generalized Pauli basis POVM $\{\tau^W_h\}_{h \in \F_q^M}$ of Chapter~\ref{chap:qpbt-algebra} and report the outcome $h$. Most subtests probe limited information about $h$: given a point $u_W \in \F_q^m$, a player is expected to report the evaluation $g_h(u_W)$ of the low-degree encoding $g_h$ of $h$, and for a fixed basis $W$ these probes are checked against each other by the classical low individual degree game of Section~\ref{sec:ld-verifier}. Consistency \emph{between} the two bases is checked through two-outcome probes: given additionally $r_W \in \F_q$, a player reports $\tr(g_h(u_W)\, r_W) \in \F_2$. The two binary measurements obtained in this way for $W = X$ and $W = Z$ either commute or anticommute, according to the value $\gamma \in \F_2$ of Equation~\eqref{eq:gamma-value} below. When $\gamma = 0$ the verifier checks commutation directly by asking for both bits simultaneously; when $\gamma = 1$ the verifier checks anticommutation by playing the Magic Square game, using Theorem~\ref{thm:ms-from-ac}.

   186	We recall the Magic Square game of Mermin and Peres. It is a simple self-test for two EPR pairs, and it allows one to test that a pair of binary observables \emph{anticommutes}; both properties are used in the Pauli basis test. Here it is presented as a binary constraint satisfaction game. Throughout this section and the next, $\sigma^X$ and $\sigma^Z$ denote the single-qubit Pauli observables, with associated two-outcome projective measurements $\{\sigma^W_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ for $W \in \{X,Z\}$.
   187	
   188	\begin{definition}[The Magic Square game]\label{def:ms-game}
   189		\uses{def:game, def:graph-distribution}
   190		The Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ is the following two-player game. There are $9$ variables $x_1,\ldots,x_9$ taking values in $\F_2$, arranged in a $3 \times 3$ grid: the cell in row $r$ and column $c$ contains the variable $x_{3(r-1)+c}$. There are $6$ linear equations over these variables: for each of the three rows and each of the first two columns, the sum of the three variables in it equals $0$; for the third column, the sum of the three variables in it equals $1$.
   191	
   192		The question types are
   193		\begin{align*}
   194			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} &= \{\mathsf{Constraint}_i : i = 1,2,\ldots,6\}\;,\\
   195			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}} &= \{\mathsf{Variable}_j : j = 1,2,\ldots,9\}\;,\\
   196			\mathcal T^{\mathrm{ms}} &= \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}} \cup \mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}\;,
   197		\end{align*}
   198		where $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ for $i \in \{1,2,3\}$ denotes the constraint of row $i$ (with variables $x_{3(i-1)+1}, x_{3(i-1)+2}, x_{3(i-1)+3}$), $\mathsf{Constraint}_4$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_5$ denote the constraints of the first two columns, and $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$ denotes the constraint of the third column (with variables $x_{i-3}, x_{i}, x_{i+3}$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$, $i \in \{4,5,6\}$).
   199	
   200		The question distribution is as follows: the verifier samples $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ uniformly from $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$, then samples $\mathsf{Variable}_j$ uniformly among the three variables appearing in the row or column of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; one player, chosen uniformly at random, receives $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and the other receives $\mathsf{Variable}_j$. Equivalently, the verifier samples a uniformly random edge of the bipartite \emph{type graph} $G^{\mathrm{ms}}$ on vertex sets $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mc}}$ and $\mathcal T^{\mathrm{mv}}$, whose edges are $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{3(i-1)+j}$ for $i,j \in \{1,2,3\}$ and $\mathsf{Constraint}_i \,\text{---}\, \mathsf{Variable}_{(i-3)+3(j-1)}$ for $i \in \{4,5,6\}$, $j \in \{1,2,3\}$ ($18$ edges in total, and no self-loops), and sends one endpoint to a uniformly random player and the other endpoint to the other player.
   201	
   202		The $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player answers with three bits $(\beta_{v_1}, \beta_{v_2}, \beta_{v_3}) \in \F_2^3$, where $(v_1,v_2,v_3)$ are the indices of the three variables of $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$; the $\mathsf{Variable}$ player answers with a single bit $\gamma \in \F_2$. The players win if and only if the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ player's answer satisfies the equation associated with $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ and $\gamma = \beta_j$.
   203	\end{definition}

   205	The following theorem records the self-testing (rigidity) properties of the Magic Square game. It is used in the soundness analysis of the Pauli basis test to enforce anticommutation relations between certain pairs of observables.
   206	
   207	\begin{theorem}[Rigidity of the Magic Square game]\label{thm:ms-rigidity}
   208		\uses{def:ms-game, def:tensor-product-value, def:EPR, def:povm-distance}
   209		Let $\mathcal S = (\ket{\psi}, A, B)$ be a strategy that succeeds in the Magic Square game $\mathfrak{G}^{\mathrm{MS}}$ with probability $1-\eps$, where $\ket{\psi} \in \hilb_{\mathrm A} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B}$. Then there exist local isometries $\phi_{\mathrm A}\colon \hilb_{\mathrm A} \to \hilb_{\mathrm A'} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm A''}$ and $\phi_{\mathrm B}\colon \hilb_{\mathrm B} \to \hilb_{\mathrm B'} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$, where $\hilb_{\mathrm A'}, \hilb_{\mathrm B'} \cong (\C^2)^{\ot 2}$ and $\hilb_{\mathrm A''}, \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$ are finite dimensional, and a state $\ket{\mathrm{aux}} \in \hilb_{\mathrm A''} \ot \hilb_{\mathrm B''}$, such that:
   210		\begin{enumerate}
   211			\item $\bigl\| \phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B} \ket{\psi} - \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\mathrm{aux}} \bigr\| \le O(\sqrt\eps)$;
   212			\item letting $\tilde A^x_a = \phi_{\mathrm A} A^x_a \phi_{\mathrm A}^\dagger$ and $\tilde B^y_b = \phi_{\mathrm B} B^y_b \phi_{\mathrm B}^\dagger$,
   213			\begin{align*}
   214				\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_b \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm A'} \ot I_{\mathrm{A''B'B''}}\;,\\
   215				\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_b \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} (\sigma^Z_b)_{\mathrm A'} \ot I_{\mathrm{A''B'B''}}\;,\\
   216				I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_b &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} I_{\mathrm{A'A''B''}} \ot (\sigma^X_b)_{\mathrm B'}\;,\\
   217				I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_b &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} I_{\mathrm{A'A''B''}} \ot (\sigma^Z_b)_{\mathrm B'}\;,
   218			\end{align*}
   219			where each $\approx_{\sqrt\eps}$ holds with respect to the state $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot 2}_{\mathrm{A'B'}} \ot \ket{\mathrm{aux}}_{\mathrm{A''B''}}$ and the answer summation is over $b \in \{0,1\}$, and the approximation bounds carry implicit universal constants.
   220		\end{enumerate}
   221		As a consequence, letting $\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} = \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_0 - \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_1$ and $\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} = \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_0 - \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_1$ denote the associated observables, it holds that
   222		\begin{align*}
   223			\tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} -\, \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} \tilde A^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} \ot I_{\mathrm{B'B''}}\;,\\
   224			I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_1} \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} &\approx_{\sqrt\eps} -\, I_{\mathrm{A'A''}} \ot \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_5} \tilde B^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}\;,
   225		\end{align*}
   226		where, for operators $M$, $N$ that are not POVM elements, the notation $M \approx_\delta N$ means $\bra{\psi} (M-N)^\dagger (M-N) \ket{\psi} \le O(\delta)$ with respect to the same state.
   227	\end{theorem}
   228	\begin{proof}
   229		This result is imported from Theorem~6.9 of~\cite{Coladangelo2017Robust}. There are two minor differences between their statement and the one given here. First, they state a robustness of $O(\eps)$, but measure the closeness of the actual and ideal states in trace norm; expressed as the Euclidean distance between $\phi_{\mathrm A} \ot \phi_{\mathrm B}\ket{\psi}$ and $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}^{\ot 2} \ot \ket{\mathrm{aux}}$, this becomes $O(\sqrt\eps)$. Second, their ideal observables for the $\mathsf{Variable}_1$ and $\mathsf{Variable}_5$ questions are $I \ot \sigma^Z$ and $\sigma^Z\sigma^X \ot \sigma^Z\sigma^X$; under a local change of basis these are equivalent to $\sigma^X \ot I$ and $\sigma^Z \ot I$, respectively.
   230	\end{proof}

   232	The converse construction shows that any pair of anticommuting binary observables yields a perfect strategy for the Magic Square game.

   234	\begin{theorem}\label{thm:ms-from-ac}
   235		\uses{def:ms-game, def:consistent-measurement, def:spcc, def:EPR, def:tensor-product-value}
   236		Let $A = \{A_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ and $B = \{B_b\}_{b \in \F_2}$ be two-outcome projective measurements acting on $(\C^q)^{\ot n}$ that are consistent on $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot n}$ (Definition~\ref{def:consistent-measurement}), and let $\mathcal O_A = A_0 - A_1$ and $\mathcal O_B = B_0 - B_1$ be the corresponding $\pm 1$-valued observables. Suppose that $\mathcal O_A \mathcal O_B = - \mathcal O_B \mathcal O_A$. Then there exists a symmetric strategy $\mathcal S = (\psi, M)$ for the Magic Square game with the following properties:
   237		\begin{enumerate}
   238			\item $\mathcal S$ is an SPCC (symmetric, projective, consistent, commuting) strategy of value $1$;
   239			\item the state is $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot n} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$;
   240			\item for $b \in \{0,1\}$, $M^{\mathsf{Variable}_1}_b = A_b \ot I$ and $M^{\mathsf{Variable}_5}_b = B_b \ot I$.
   241		\end{enumerate}
   242	\end{theorem}
   243	\begin{proof}
   244		\uses{def:consistent-measurement}
   245		The strategy is based on the canonical two-qubit operator solution of the Magic Square, with the state $\ket{\psi} = \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot n} \ot \ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$ and the cells of the grid assigned the $\pm 1$-valued observables
   246		\[
   247			\begin{array}{ccc}
   248				\mathcal O_A \ot I & I \ot \sigma^X & \mathcal O_A \ot \sigma^X \\[2pt]
   249				I \ot \sigma^Z & \mathcal O_B \ot I & \mathcal O_B \ot \sigma^Z \\[2pt]
   250				\mathcal O_A \ot \sigma^Z & \mathcal O_B \ot \sigma^X & \mathcal O_A \mathcal O_B \ot \sigma^Z \sigma^X
   251			\end{array}
   252		\]
   253		on $(\C^q)^{\ot n} \ot \C^2$: on question $\mathsf{Variable}_j$ a player measures the two-outcome projective measurement of the observable in cell $j$, and on question $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ a player simultaneously performs the three measurements of the corresponding row or column; item~3 holds by construction. Anticommutation of $\mathcal O_A$ and $\mathcal O_B$ gives
   254		\begin{equation}\label{eq:am-i-hermitian}
   255			\mathcal O_A \mathcal O_B \ot \sigma^Z \sigma^X
   256			= - \mathcal O_A \mathcal O_B \ot \sigma^X \sigma^Z
   257			= \mathcal O_B \mathcal O_A \ot \sigma^X \sigma^Z
   258			= (\mathcal O_A \mathcal O_B \ot \sigma^Z \sigma^X)^\dagger\;,
   259		\end{equation}
   260		so the bottom-right cell is Hermitian, and it squares to the identity; hence every cell is a genuine $\pm 1$-valued observable. The three observables in each row and each column commute pairwise --- for the third row and third column this again uses Equation~\eqref{eq:am-i-hermitian} --- so the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ measurements are well defined, and the strategy is symmetric, projective, and commuting. A two-outcome projective measurement is consistent on a state if and only if its observable $\mathcal O$ satisfies $\mathcal O \ot I \ket{\psi} = I \ot \mathcal O \ket{\psi}$; since $A$ and $B$ are consistent on $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_q}^{\ot n}$ by hypothesis and $\sigma^X$, $\sigma^Z$ are consistent on $\ket{\mathrm{EPR}_2}$, each cell observable is a product of consistent, commuting factors and is therefore consistent on $\ket{\psi}$, and consistency of the $\mathsf{Constraint}$ measurements follows from the cellwise consistencies together with commutativity. Finally, the observables in each row and each of the first two columns multiply to $I$, while those of the third column multiply to $-I$; for the measurement $\{S_0, S_1\}$ obtained by measuring a $\mathsf{Constraint}_i$ triple and outputting the sum of the three bits, the observable $S_0 - S_1$ equals the product of the three cell observables, hence $\pm I$, which forces the three answer bits to sum to $0$ (respectively, $1$ for $\mathsf{Constraint}_6$) with certainty. Together with consistency this shows that every check of the Magic Square game is passed with probability $1$, so the strategy has value $1$.

import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.ParametersBase
import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix
import Mathlib

/-!
# Distribution infrastructure for the low individual degree test

Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,
a probability predicate, push-forward distributions, weighted-sum linear maps,
averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.

Note: this module contributes declarations to the comparator statement closure
of `mainFormal`, which must elaborate in the same environment as the
Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not narrow
it.  See `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment".
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
  support : Finset α := ∅
  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl

namespace Distribution

/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a

/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
  𝒟.totalWeight = 1

/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.

This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
  support := 𝒟.support.image e
  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim

@[simp]
theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl

@[simp]
theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl

/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩) 𝒟.weight)

/-- A finite weighted sum over a push-forward distribution is the corresponding
weighted sum of the pulled-back family.  This is the `Distribution` analogue of
the finite-sum form of `PMF.map`. -/
theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :
    ∑ b ∈ (𝒟.map e).support, (𝒟.map e).weight b • f b =
      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
  classical
  calc
    ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
        (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a) • f b
        = ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
            ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
          intro b _
          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
          intro a ha
          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm
    _ = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
          exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
            (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)
            (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • f (e a))

end Distribution

/-- On a finite ambient type, a summand that vanishes outside a distribution's
explicit support has the same total sum over all ambient values as over that support.

This is a project-local explicit-support adapter around Mathlib's `Finset.sum_subset`:
Mathlib supplies the finite-sum theorem, while this lemma packages the common shape used
when paper expressions sum over a whole question set but the repository stores a smaller
`Distribution.support`.  It is not intended to replace Mathlib probability theory. -/
theorem Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
    [AddCommMonoid β] (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β)
    (hf : ∀ a, a ∉ 𝒟.support → f a = 0) :
    (∑ a : α, f a) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, f a := by
  classical
  simpa using
    (Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
      (fun a _ ha => hf a ha)).symm

namespace Distribution.IsProbability

/-- Unpack the equality form of the probability invariant. -/
theorem weight_sum_eq_one {α : Type*}
    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight] using h𝒟

/-- On a finite ambient type, a probabilistic `Distribution` has total weight `1` even
when its weights are summed over the whole ambient type.

This packages the explicit-support bookkeeping in `Distribution` for downstream Lean
statements that follow the paper's notation `𝔼_{x ∼ 𝒟}` over the question set rather
than over a stored support finset. -/
theorem weight_sum_univ_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
    (∑ a : α, 𝒟.weight a) = 1 := by
  rw [Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support 𝒟 𝒟.weight 𝒟.outsideSupport]
  exact h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one

/-- A probability distribution has total weight at most `1`. -/
theorem weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*}
    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a ≤ 1 :=
  le_of_eq h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one

/-- Push-forward preserves the probability invariant. -/
theorem map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
    (𝒟.map e).IsProbability := by
  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.map_totalWeight] using h𝒟

end Distribution.IsProbability

namespace Distribution

/-- The Mathlib probability mass function associated to a project `Distribution`
whose total mass is one.

The construction sends each nonnegative real weight to `ℝ≥0∞` by
`ENNReal.ofReal`; the hypotheses of `PMF.ofFinset` are exactly the project
probability invariant and the stored zero-off-support condition. -/
noncomputable def toPMF {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) : PMF α :=
  PMF.ofFinset (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a)) 𝒟.support
    (by
      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a),
        h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one]
      simp)
    (by
      intro a ha
      rw [𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
      simp)

@[simp]
theorem toPMF_apply {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a) := rfl

@[simp]
theorem toPMF_apply_toReal {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
    (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal = 𝒟.weight a := by
  rw [toPMF_apply, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (𝒟.nonnegative a)]

/-- The associated PMF has zero mass outside the stored support of the project
distribution. -/
theorem toPMF_apply_of_notMem {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {a : α} (ha : a ∉ 𝒟.support) :
    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = 0 := by
  rw [toPMF_apply, 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
  simp

/-- The project push-forward agrees with Mathlib's push-forward of the
associated probability mass function. -/
theorem toPMF_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
    (𝒟.map e).toPMF (h𝒟.map e) = (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟).map e := by
  classical
  ext b
  rw [toPMF_apply, PMF.map_apply, map_weight]
  rw [ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg
    (s := 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b))
    (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a)]
  rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := 𝒟.support)]
  · rw [Finset.sum_filter]
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro a ha
    by_cases hea : e a = b
    · have hba : b = e a := hea.symm
      rw [if_pos hea, if_pos hba, toPMF_apply]
    · have hba : b ≠ e a := fun hba => hea hba.symm
      rw [if_neg hea, if_neg hba]
  · intro a ha
    by_cases hba : b = e a
    · rw [if_pos hba, toPMF_apply_of_notMem 𝒟 h𝒟 ha]
    · rw [if_neg hba]

end Distribution

/-- Average a scalar function against the stored finite support of a distribution. -/
def avgOver {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error) : Error :=
  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a
import MIPStarRE.LDT.Basic.DistributionAvg

/-!
# Uniform subset estimates

This file contains estimates for the total variation distance between the
uniform distribution on a finite type and the uniform distribution on a
nonempty finite subset, together with averaging bounds for `[0,1]`-valued
functions.  The uniform-subset total-variation identity is proved by transport
through Mathlib probability mass functions.
-/

open scoped BigOperators

namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

/-- Total variation between the uniform distribution on a finite ambient type and
the uniform distribution on a nonempty finite subset.

This is the elementary finite identity
`TV(uniform α, uniform s) = 1 - |s| / |α|`.  The proof transports the project
`Distribution` statement to Mathlib's uniform probability mass functions. -/
theorem totalVariationDistance_uniformDistribution_uniformOnFinset_eq
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    totalVariationDistance (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) =
      1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
  rw [totalVariationDistance_eq_toPMF_sum]
  change PMF.totalVariationDistance
      ((uniformDistribution α).toPMF (uniformDistribution_isProbability α))
      ((Distribution.uniformOnFinset s).toPMF
        (Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs)) =
    1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error)
  rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_toPMF]
  exact PMF.totalVariationDistance_uniformOfFintype_uniformOfFinset_eq s hs

/-- A `[0,1]`-valued function averaged over a nonempty finite subset is bounded
by its ambient uniform average plus the total variation distance between the
two uniform distributions. -/
theorem avgOver_uniformOnFinset_le_uniformDistribution_add_totalVariationDistance
    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty)
    (f : α → Error)
    (hf_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f a)
    (hf_le_one : ∀ a, f a ≤ 1) :
    avgOver (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) f
      ≤ avgOver (uniformDistribution α) f
        + totalVariationDistance (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) := by
  exact
    avgOver_le_avgOver_add_totalVariationDistance
      (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s)
      (uniformDistribution_isProbability α)
      (Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs)
      f hf_nonneg hf_le_one

end MIPStarRE.LDT

import MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix.NormalizedTrace

/-!
# Matrix-valued measurements for the MIP*=RE project

This file provides the matrix-valued measurement layer used by the LDT formalization.

## Main definitions

* `Submeasurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to at most the identity.
* `Measurement` — a family of PSD matrices summing to exactly the identity.
* `Submeasurement.postprocess` — data-processed submeasurements via answer relabeling.
* `Measurement.postprocess` — the paper's postprocessing proposition for complete POVMs.
* `inconsistency` — the off-diagonal mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`.
* `diagOverlap` — the diagonal mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`.

## References

This file builds the project's finite-dimensional measurement layer on top of
the normalized-trace and positive-operator facts in `MIPStarRE.Quantum.FiniteMatrix`
for the quantum formalization in `references/ldt-paper/`.
-/

open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder

namespace MIPStarRE.Quantum

/-! ## Submeasurements and measurements -/

/--
A submeasurement on a finite answer type `α` is a family of PSD matrices
`M : α → Op d` with `∑ a, M a ≤ 1`.
-/
structure Submeasurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d] where
  /-- The effect operators. -/
  effect : α → Op d
  /-- Each effect is positive semidefinite. -/
  pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a
  /-- The effects sum to at most the identity. -/
  sum_le_one : ∑ a, effect a ≤ 1

/--
A measurement is a submeasurement whose effects sum exactly to the identity.
-/
structure Measurement (α : Type*) [Fintype α] (d : Type*) [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
    extends Submeasurement α d where
  /-- The effects sum to the identity. -/
  sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1

/-! ## Totals and postprocessing -/

namespace Submeasurement

variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]

/-! ### Totals and postprocessing -/

/-- The total operator `∑ a, M_a`. -/
noncomputable def total (M : Submeasurement α d) : Op d :=
  ∑ a, M.effect a

/--
Data processing: relabel the answer set by `f : α → β`, summing the effects over
fibers.
-/
noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) : Submeasurement β d where
  effect b := ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
  pos b := Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => M.pos a
  sum_le_one := by
    calc
      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
      _ ≤ 1 := M.sum_le_one

/-- Restatement of `sum_le_one` in terms of the named total operator. -/
theorem total_le_one (M : Submeasurement α d) :
    M.total ≤ 1 := by
  simpa [total] using M.sum_le_one

/-- Postprocessing preserves the sum of all effects. -/
theorem postprocess_sum_eq [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    ∑ a, M.effect a = ∑ b, (M.postprocess f).effect b :=
  (Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect).symm

/-- Postprocessing preserves the named total operator. -/
theorem postprocess_total [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Submeasurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    (M.postprocess f).total = M.total := by
  simpa [total] using (M.postprocess_sum_eq f).symm

end Submeasurement

namespace Measurement

variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
variable {α β : Type*} [Fintype α] [Fintype β]

/--
Build a complete measurement from effects whose sum is exactly the identity.

This constructor keeps the equality proof as the primary hypothesis and derives
the inherited submeasurement inequality automatically.  It is useful at paper
sites that are explicitly POVMs rather than relaxed sub-POVMs.
-/
def ofSumEqOne (effect : α → Op d) (pos : ∀ a, 0 ≤ effect a)
    (sum_eq_one : ∑ a, effect a = 1) : Measurement α d where
  effect := effect
  pos := pos
  sum_le_one := le_of_eq sum_eq_one
  sum_eq_one := sum_eq_one

/-- The named total of a complete measurement is the identity. -/
theorem total_eq_one (M : Measurement α d) :
    M.total = 1 :=
  M.sum_eq_one

/--
Postprocess a complete measurement by relabeling outcomes.

This formalizes `references/ldt-paper/preliminaries.tex:169--180`: regrouping
the effects along the fibers of `f` preserves the total operator, so a POVM
remains a POVM after postprocessing.
-/
noncomputable def postprocess [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) : Measurement β d where
  toSubmeasurement := M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f
  sum_eq_one := by
    calc
      ∑ b, ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a
          = ∑ a, M.effect a := Finset.sum_fiberwise Finset.univ f M.effect
      _ = 1 := M.sum_eq_one

@[simp] theorem postprocess_effect [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) (b : β) :
    (M.postprocess f).effect b =
      ∑ a ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun a => f a = b), M.effect a :=
  rfl

@[simp] theorem postprocess_to_submeasurement [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    (M : Measurement α d) (f : α → β) :
    (M.postprocess f).toSubmeasurement = M.toSubmeasurement.postprocess f :=
  rfl

end Measurement

/-! ## Overlap definitions -/

section Overlap

variable {d : Type*} [Fintype d] [DecidableEq d]
variable {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]

/-- The off-diagonal overlap mass `∑_{a ≠ b} τ(M_a N_b)`. -/
noncomputable def inconsistency (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
  ∑ a, ∑ b ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun b => b ≠ a), normalizedTrace (M a * N b)

/-- The diagonal overlap mass `∑_a τ(M_a N_a)`. -/
noncomputable def diagOverlap (M N : α → Op d) : ℂ :=
  ∑ a, normalizedTrace (M a * N a)

end Overlap

end MIPStarRE.Quantum

   528	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   529	    PauliQuestion P → PauliQuestion P → PauliAnswer P → PauliAnswer P → Bool :=
   530	  open Classical in
   531	  fun (tA, xA) (tB, xB) a b =>
   532	    if validPauliAnswer tA a && validPauliAnswer tB b then
   533	      match tA, tB, a, b with
   534	      | .point W, .point W', .value u, .value v =>
   535	          decide (W = W' ∧ u = v)
   536	      | .aline W, .point W', .alinePoly f, .value u =>
   537	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliAlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u)
   538	      | .point W, .aline W', .value u, .alinePoly f =>
   539	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u)
   540	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   541	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u)
   542	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   543	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u)
   544	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   545	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u)
   546	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   547	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u)
   548	      | .pairW W, .pair, .bit β, .pairBits bits =>
   549	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   550	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   551	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   552	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   553	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β)
   554	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   555	          decide (W = W' ∧ pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β)
   556	      | .ms t, .ms t', .msTriple u, .msTriple v =>
   557	          decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   558	            msWinPredicate t t' (.triple u) (.triple v))
   559	      | .ms t, .ms t', .bit u, .bit v =>
   560	          decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   561	            msWinPredicate t t' (.bit u) (.bit v))
   562	      | .point W, .ms (.var j), .value u, .bit β =>
   563	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   564	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   565	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)
   566	      | .aline W, .aline W', .alinePoly f, .alinePoly g => decide (W = W' ∧ f = g)
   567	      | .dline W, .dline W', .dlinePoly f, .dlinePoly g => decide (W = W' ∧ f = g)
   568	      | .pauli W, .pauli W', .pauliOutcome u, .pauliOutcome v =>
   569	          decide (W = W' ∧ u = v)
   570	      | .pairW W, .pairW W', .bit u, .bit v => decide (W = W' ∧ u = v)
   571	      | .pair, .pair, .pairBits u, .pairBits v => decide (u = v)
   572	      | _, _, _, _ => true
   573	    else false

  1426	\paragraph{Soundness of the Pauli basis test.} 
  1427	We state the soundness properties of the Pauli basis test.
  1428	The following is an adaptation of the self-testing statement in~\cite[Theorem
  1429	6.4]{NW19}.
  1430	
  1431	\begin{theorem}
  1432	  \label{thm:pauli}
  1433	There exists a function 
  1434	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
  1435	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
  1436	\begin{enumerate}
  1437	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
  1438	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
  1439	    \begin{gather*}
  1440	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
  1441	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,

   182	def embedLd (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
   183	    (u : LdSpace P.toLdParams) : PauliSpace P :=

   185	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) =>
   186	      match W with
   187	      | .X => u (.inl (.inl j))
   188	      | .Z => 0
   189	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) =>
   190	      match W with
   191	      | .X => 0
   192	      | .Z => u (.inl (.inl j))

   194	  | .inl (.inl (.inr j)) => u (.inr j)
   195	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   196	  | .inr _ => 0

   198	/-- The type-4 projection retaining `V_X`, `V_Z`, `V_{R_X}`, and `V_{R_Z}` from

   202	def pauliSharedProjection (z : PauliSpace P) : PauliSpace P :=
   203	  fun i => match i with
   204	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl j)))))
   205	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))) => z (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j)))))
   206	  | .inl (.inl (.inl (.inr _))) => 0
   207	  | .inl (.inl (.inr _)) => 0
   208	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   209	  | .inr _ => z (.inr ())

   211	/-- The source level attached to each typed Pauli CL map.  This records the
   212	exact levels in items 1--5 of `def:pauli-question-distribution`: point, line,
   213	and diagonal maps have levels 1, 2, and 3, the Pauli map has level 0, and the
   214	shared projection has level 1.  Blueprint
   215	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`; paper origin
   216	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`.
   217	-/
   218	def pauliCLLevel : PauliType → ℕ
   219	  | .point _ => 1
   220	  | .aline _ => 2
   221	  | .dline _ => 3
   222	  | .pauli _ => 0
   223	  | .pairW _ => 1
   224	  | .pair => 1
   225	  | .ms _ => 1

   227	/-- The typed CL dispatcher.  The point/line maps are the corresponding
   228	low-degree maps embedded in the selected basis block; Pair, Magic Square, and
   229	Pair/W types use the shared projection; Pauli/W is the zero-level map.  This
   230	is the direct finite-space form of `def:pauli-question-distribution`,
   231	blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`, paper origin
   232	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1010`.

   234	noncomputable def pauliCL (P : AdmissibleParams) (t : PauliType) :
   235	    PauliSpace P → PauliSpace P :=
   236	  match t with
   237	  | .point W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldPointCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   238	  | .aline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldALineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   239	  | .dline W => fun z => embedLd P W (ldDLineCL P.toLdParams (pauliToLd P W z))
   240	  | .pauli _ => fun _ => 0
   241	  | .pairW _ => pauliSharedProjection
   242	  | .pair => pauliSharedProjection
   243	  | .ms _ => pauliSharedProjection

   255	the displayed type-incidence families are the graph used by the sampler in
   256	`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint lines 285-329, paper origin

   258	-/
   259	def pauliEdges : Finset (Sym2 PauliType) :=
   260	  let loops := Finset.univ.image (fun t : PauliType => Sym2.mk t t)
   261	  let lineEdges :=
   262	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   263	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.aline W)) ∪
   264	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   265	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.dline W)) ∪
   266	      (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   267	        Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pauli W))
   268	  let basisEdges :=
   269	    (Finset.univ : Finset PauliKind).image (fun W =>
   270	      Sym2.mk (.point W) (.pairW W)) ∪
   271	      ({Sym2.mk (.point .X) (.ms (.var ⟨0, by decide⟩)),
   272	        Sym2.mk (.point .Z) (.ms (.var ⟨4, by decide⟩))} : Finset (Sym2 PauliType))

   275	      Sym2.mk (.pairW W) .pair)

   279	        Sym2.mk (.ms xy.1) (.ms xy.2))

     5	/-!
     6	# The Magic Square game
     7	
     8	The Magic Square component is represented by finite constraint and variable
     9	question types, the incidence graph, and the two corresponding answer forms.
    10	Its rigidity theorem is outside the stage-4.1 statement closure; only the game
    11	carrier is needed here.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	This file formalizes `def:ms-game` in
    16	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, from
    17	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    21	
    22	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    23	
    24	/-- A Magic Square question is either a row/column constraint or a cell
    25	variable.  This is `def:ms-game`, blueprint lines 188-203, paper origin
    26	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    27	-/
    28	inductive MsType where
    29	  | constraint (i : Fin 6)
    30	  | var (j : Fin 9)
    31	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    32	
    33	/-- The cell incident to a constraint and one of its three positions in
    34	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    36	-/
    37	def msConstraintVars (i : Fin 6) (j : Fin 3) : Fin 9 :=
    38	  ⟨if i.val < 3 then i.val * 3 + j.val else i.val - 3 + j.val * 3, by
    39	    by_cases h : i.val < 3 <;> simp [h] <;> omega⟩
    40	
    41	/-- The exceptional Magic Square parity, equal to one only on the final
    42	constraint.  Blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`; paper
    43	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    44	-/
    45	def msParity (i : Fin 6) : ZMod 2 :=
    46	  if i.val = 5 then 1 else 0
    47	
    48	/-- The 18 constraint-variable incidence edges of the Magic Square graph in
    49	`def:ms-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    50	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    51	-/
    52	def msEdges : Finset (Sym2 MsType) :=
    53	  (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin 6 × Fin 3)).image (fun ij =>
    54	    Sym2.mk (.constraint ij.1) (.var (msConstraintVars ij.1 ij.2)))
    55	
    56	/-- A Magic Square answer is a parity triple or a single cell bit, as prescribed
    57	by `def:ms-game`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`,
    58	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    59	-/
    60	inductive MsAnswer where
    61	  | triple (β : Fin 3 → ZMod 2)
    62	  | bit (γ : ZMod 2)
    63	  deriving DecidableEq
    64	
    65	/-- A finite code for the two Magic Square answer constructors.  This is
    66	Lean-only carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    67	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    68	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    69	-/
    70	abbrev MsAnswerCode := (Fin 3 → ZMod 2) ⊕ ZMod 2
    71	
    72	/-- The constructor-preserving code equivalence for `MsAnswer`; Lean-only
    73	finite-carrier infrastructure for `def:ms-game`, blueprint
    74	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
    76	-/
    77	noncomputable def msAnswerEquiv : MsAnswer ≃ MsAnswerCode where
    78	  toFun
    79	    | .triple β => .inl β
    80	    | .bit γ => .inr γ
    81	  invFun
    82	    | .inl β => .triple β
    83	    | .inr γ => .bit γ
    84	  left_inv := by intro x; cases x <;> rfl
    85	  right_inv := by
    86	    intro x
    87	    cases x <;> rfl
    88	
    89	noncomputable instance : Fintype MsAnswer :=
    90	  Fintype.ofEquiv MsAnswerCode msAnswerEquiv.symm
    91	
    92	instance : Inhabited MsAnswer := ⟨.bit 0⟩
    93	
    94	/-- The Magic Square consistency predicate.  Constructor mismatches are
    95	rejected, as required by `def:ms-game` (blueprint lines 188-203; paper
    96	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`).
    97	-/
    98	def msWinPredicate :
    99	    MsType → MsType → MsAnswer → MsAnswer → Bool
   100	  | .constraint i, .constraint j, .triple β, .triple β' =>
   101	      decide (i = j ∧ β = β')
   102	  | .var i, .var j, .bit γ, .bit γ' =>
   103	      decide (i = j ∧ γ = γ')
   104	  | .constraint i, .var j, .triple β, .bit γ =>
   105	      decide
   106	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   107	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   108	  | .var j, .constraint i, .bit γ, .triple β =>
   109	      decide
   110	        ((∑ k : Fin 3, β k) = msParity i ∧
   111	          ∃ k : Fin 3, msConstraintVars i k = j ∧ β k = γ)
   112	  | _, _, _, _ => false
   113	
   114	/-- The Magic Square game as a finite `Game`.  This is `def:ms-game` in
   115	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:188-203`, paper origin
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1050-1069`.
   117	-/
   118	noncomputable def msGame : Game where
   119	  QuestionA := MsType
   120	  QuestionB := MsType
   121	  AnswerA := MsAnswer
   122	  AnswerB := MsAnswer
   123	  μ := graphDistribution msEdges
   124	  μ_prob := by sorry
   125	  decide := msWinPredicate
   126	
   127	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    12	stage-4.1 skeleton; the carriers below are concrete finite-dimensional vectors
    13	and matrices so that later proofs can use the existing Hilbert-space API.

    17	The main declaration is `thm:pauli` in
    18	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:386-403`, with paper origin
    19	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1426-1447`.

    31	/-- The Pauli-test error scale.  The argument order is `(a, b, ε, m, d, q)`;
    32	the powers are real `rpow`s and the asymptotic constants are absorbed into `a`,

    36	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
    37	  a * Real.rpow ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) a *
    38	    (Real.rpow ε b + Real.rpow (q : ℝ) (-b) +
    39	      Real.rpow 2 (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))

    41	/-- Matrix conjugation by a finite-dimensional linear isometry.  This is a

    47	noncomputable def conjIsometry {ι ι' : Type*}

    49	    (φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ ι')
    50	    (M : Op ι) : Op ι' :=
    51	  let U : Matrix ι' ι ℂ := Matrix.toEuclideanLin.symm φ.toLinearMap

    54	/-- Reindex a finite Euclidean-space vector along an equivalence.  This is the

    60	    [Fintype ι'] [DecidableEq ι'] (e : ι ≃ ι')
    61	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι' :=
    62	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι' ℂ).symm
    63	    (fun j => (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ ψ) (e.symm j))

    71	noncomputable def isometryTensor
    72	    {ιA ιB ιA' ιB' R : Type*}
    73	    [Fintype ιA] [DecidableEq ιA] [Fintype ιB] [DecidableEq ιB]
    74	    [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA'] [Fintype ιB'] [DecidableEq ιB']
    75	    [Fintype R] [DecidableEq R]
    76	    (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × R))
    77	    (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ] EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × R))

    79	    EuclideanSpace ℂ ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) :=
    80	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ((ιA' × R) × (ιB' × R)) ℂ).symm

   113	/-- The A-side ideal Pauli projector, with identities on the auxiliary and

   118	noncomputable def pauliProjOnA'' (P : AdmissibleParams)
   119	    {ιA' ιB' : Type*} [Fintype ιA'] [DecidableEq ιA']

   136	    Op ((ιA' × PauliRegister P) × (ιB' × PauliRegister P)) :=

   653	\subsubsection{Bit string representations}
   654	\label{sec:ff-representations}
   655	
   656	As mentioned at the end of \Cref{sec:tms}, we sometimes treat the
   657	inputs and outputs of Turing machines as representing elements of a finite
   658	field, or a vector space over a finite field.
   659	We discuss some important details about bit representations of finite field
   660	elements and arithmetic over finite fields.
   661	
   662	In the paper we only consider fields $\F_{2^k}$ where $k$ is odd. 
   663	
   664	\begin{definition}\label{def:admissible-size}
   665	  A field size $q$ is called an \emph{admissible} field size if $q=2^k$ for odd
   666	  $k$.
   667	\end{definition}
   668	
   669	Elements of $\F_2$ are naturally represented using bits. 
   670	To represent elements of $\F_{2^k}$ as binary strings we require the
   671	specification of a basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.
   672	Given a basis $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ of $\F_{2^k}$, every element $a \in \F_{2^k}$
   673	has a unique expansion $a = \sum_{i=1}^k a_i e_i$ and can be represented as the
   674	$k$-bit string corresponding to $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$.
   675	Note that we omitted the subscript $2$ of $\downsize$ as it maps to the linear
   676	space over the prime subfield $\F_2$.
   677	Thus the \emph{binary representation} of $a \in \F_{2^k}$ is defined as the
   678	natural binary representation of $\downsize(a) \in \F_2^k$ (which in turn is the
   679	\emph{$\F_2$-representation of $a$}).
   680	Throughout the paper we freely associate between the binary representation of a
   681	field element $a \in \F_{2^k}$ and its $\F_2$-representation,
   682	although---technically speaking---these are distinct objects.
   683	
   684	Given the representations $\downsize(a), \downsize(b)$ of $a, b \in \F_{2^k}$, to
   685	compute the binary representation of $a+b$ it suffices to compute the addition
   686	bit-wise, modulo $2$.
   687	Computing the multiplication of elements $a, b$ requires the specification of
   688	the multiplication tables $\{K_{e_i} \in \Matrix_k (\F_2)\}_{i=1}^k $ for the
   689	basis $\{e_i\}$.
   690	Given representations $\downsize(a) = (a_i)_{i=1}^k$, $\downsize(b) =
   691	(b_i)_{i=1}^k$ for $a, b \in \F_{2^k}$ respectively, the representation
   692	$\downsize(ab)$ of the product $ab$ is computed as
   693	\begin{equation}
   694	  \label{eq:eq-mult}
   695	  \downsize(ab) = \sum_{i=1}^k \, a_i \, \downsize \bigl( e_i b \bigr) =
   696	  \sum_{i=1}^k \, a_i \bigl( K_{e_i}\, \downsize (b) \bigr)\;.
   697	\end{equation}
   698	Thus, using our representation for field elements, efficiently performing finite
   699	field arithmetic in $\F_{2^k}$ reduces to having access to the multiplication
   700	table of some basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.
   701	
   702	The following fact provides an efficient deterministic algorithm for computing a
   703	self-dual normal basis for $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ and the corresponding
   704	multiplication tables for any odd $k$.
   705	
   706	\begin{lemma}
   707	  \label{lem:efficient_basis}
   708	  There exists a deterministic algorithm that given an odd integer $k > 0$,
   709	  outputs a self-dual normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$ and the
   710	  multiplication tables of the basis in $\poly(k)$ time.
   711	\end{lemma}
   712	
   713	\begin{proof}
   714		The algorithm of Shoup~\cite[Theorem 3.2]{shoup1990new} shows that for prime
   715	  $p$, an irreducible polynomial in $\Fp[X]$ of degree $k$ can be computed in
   716	  time $\poly(p, k)$.
   717	  Then, the algorithm of Lenstra~\cite[Theorem 1.1]{lenstra1991finding} shows
   718	  that given such an irreducible polynomial, the multiplication table of a
   719	  normal basis of $\F_{p^k}$ over $\Fp$ can be computed in $\poly(k,\log p)$
   720	  time.
   721	  Finally, the algorithm of Wang~\cite{wang1989algorithm} shows that for odd $k$
   722	  and a multiplication table $K$ of a normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$, a
   723	  multiplication table $K'$ for a self-dual normal basis of $\F_{2^k}$ over
   724	  $\F_2$ can be computed in $\poly(k)$ time.
   725	  Putting these three algorithms together yields the claimed statement.
   726	\end{proof}
   727	
   728	For $q=2^k$ for $k$ odd (i.e.\ $q$ is an admissible field size) we use the shorthand $\tr$ for $\tr_{q\to 2}$.
   729	
   730	\begin{lemma}
   731	  \label{lem:one}
   732	  Let $k$ be an odd integer and $\{e_i\}_{i=1}^k$ be a self-dual normal basis of
   733	  $\F_{2^k}$ over $\F_2$.
   734	  Then $\tr(e_i) = 1$ for all $i$, and furthermore the representation
   735	  $\downsize(1)$ of the unit $1 \in \F_{2^k}$ is the all ones vector in
   736	  $\F_2^k$.
   737	\end{lemma}
   738	
   739	\begin{proof}
   740	  Since $\{e_i \}$ is a normal basis, $e_i = \alpha^{2^i}$ for some element
   741	  $\alpha \in \F_{2^k}$.
   742	  Furthermore, for every element $b \in \F_{2^k}$, we have that $\tr(b^2) =
   743	  \tr(b)$.
   744	  This is because
   745	  \[
   746	    \tr(b^2) = \sum_{i=0}^{k-1} b^{2^{i+1}} =
   747	    \sum_{i = 0}^{k-1} b^{2^i} = \tr(b)\;,
   748	  \]
   749	  where we use that $b^{2^k} = b$ for all $b \in \F_{2^k}$.
   750	  Since $e_{i+1} = e_i^2$, we get that $\tr(e_i) = \tr(e_j)$ for all $i,j$.
   751	  It cannot be the case that $\tr(e_i) = 0$ for all $i$.
   752	  Suppose that this were the case.
   753	  This would imply that $\tr(b) = 0$ for all $b \in \F_{2^k}$.
   754	  But then for all $j \in \{1, \ldots, k\}$ and for some $b \neq 0$, we would
   755	  also have by item 1 of \Cref{lem:downsize_field} that $b_j = \tr(b e_j) = 0$ where $b = \sum_j b_j e_j$ with $b_j \in
   756	  \F_2$.
   757	  This implies that $b$ is the all zero element of $\F_{2^k}$, which is a
   758	  contradiction.
   759	  Thus $\tr(e_i) = 1$ for all $i=1, 2, \ldots, k$.

    57	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear functions]
    58	  Let $\type$ be a finite set and $V$ be $\F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
    59	  A \emph{$\type$-typed family of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions}
    60	  (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is a collection $\{L_\tvar\}_{\tvar \in \type}$
    61	  such that, for each $\tvar \in \type$, $L_\tvar$ is an $\ell$-level
    62	  conditionally linear function on~$V$.
    63	\end{definition}
    64	
    65	\begin{definition}[Graph distribution]
    66	  \label{def:graph-distribution}
    67	  Let $G = (U, E)$ be an undirected graph with vertex set $U$ and edge set~$E$.
    68	  Edges in~$E$ are written as multisets $\{u, v\}$ of two vertices; the case $u
    69	  = v$ represents a self-loop.
    70	  Suppose there are $m$ edges, $k$ of which are self-loops.
    71	  Then the \emph{graph distribution $\mu_G$ of~$G$} is the distribution over
    72	  $U\times U$ such that for every $(u, v)\in U\times U$,
    73	  \begin{equation*}
    74	    \mu_G(u, v) =
    75	    \begin{cases}
    76	      1/(2m-k) & \text{if $\{u, v\} \in E$},\\
    77	      0 & \text{otherwise}.
    78	    \end{cases}
    79	  \end{equation*}
    80	  This is identical to the uniform distribution over pairs $(u, v)\in U\times U$
    81	  such that $\{u, v\} \in E$.
    82	\end{definition}
    83	
    84	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear distributions]
    85	  Let $\type$ be a type set and
    86	  $L=\{L_\lvar\}_{\lvar\in\type},R=\{R_\rvar\}_{\rvar\in\type}$ be $\type$-typed
    87	  families of conditionally linear functions on~$V$.
    88	  Let $G = (\type, E)$ be a graph with vertex set $\type$.
    89	  The \emph{$(\type, G)$-typed conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,\,
    90	      R}^G$ corresponding to~$(L, R)$} is the distribution over pairs $( (\lvar,
    91	  x), (\rvar, y) )$, where $(\lvar, \rvar)$ is drawn from $\mu_G$ and $(x,y)$ is
    92	  drawn from $\mu_{L_\lvar,\, R_\rvar}$.
    93	\end{definition}

    95	\begin{definition}[Typed conditionally linear samplers]
    96	  \label{def:typed-sampler}
    97		Let $q:\N \to \N$ be an admissible field size function and $s: \N \to \N$ be a

    32	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    33	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2

    35	private noncomputable def applyOperatorToState {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    36	    (M : Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι :=
    37	  (EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm (M.mulVec ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ) ψ))

    45	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    46	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    47	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    48	  avgOver μ (fun x =>

   151	## (d) Statement sketch of `MIPStarRE.QPBT.pauli_soundness`
   152	
   153	```lean
   154	/-- Soundness function of the Pauli basis test; argument order (ε, m, d, q)
   155	everywhere, per rem:delta-qld-argument-order. Real rpow throughout. -/
   156	noncomputable def deltaQld (a b ε : ℝ) (m d q : ℕ) : ℝ :=
   157	  a * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ) ^ a *
   158	    (ε ^ b + (q : ℝ) ^ (-b) + (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(b * ((m * d : ℕ) : ℝ))))
   159	
   160	/-- thm:pauli (qpbt-paper 08_…tex:1426-1447): soundness of the Pauli basis test. -/
   161	theorem pauli_soundness :
   162	    ∃ a b : ℝ, 1 ≤ a ∧ 0 < b ∧ b < 1 ∧
   163	      ∀ (P : AdmissibleParams) [FieldModel P.q] (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε →
   164	        ∀ S : Strategy (pauliBasisTest P), 1 - ε ≤ S.value →
   165	          ∃ (ιA' ιB' : Type) (_ : Fintype ιA') (_ : DecidableEq ιA')
   166	            (_ : Fintype ιB') (_ : DecidableEq ιB')
   167	            (φA : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιA →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   168	                    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × PauliRegister P))
   169	            (φB : EuclideanSpace ℂ S.ιB →ₗᵢ[ℂ]
   170	                    EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   171	            (aux : EuclideanSpace ℂ (ιA' × ιB')), ‖aux‖ = 1 ∧
   172	            -- item 1: ‖φA ⊗ φB ψ − aux ⊗ EPR_q^{⊗M}‖ ≤ δ_qld  (squared distance,
   173	            -- via stateDistSq and deltaQld²; or state with ‖·‖ directly — either
   174	            -- form is acceptable, document the choice)
   175	            ‖isometryTensor φA φB S.ψ - idealState P aux‖
   176	                ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   177	            -- item 2, for both players and both bases, summation over u ∈ F_q^M,
   178	            -- w.r.t. the ideal state; O(·) constants absorbed into a (see (e)8)
   179	            ∀ W : PauliKind,
   180	              (∑ u : PauliRegister P,
   181	                ‖(heteroKron
   182	                    (conjIsometry φA ((S.A (pauliQuestion P W)).effect
   183	                      (PauliAnswer.pauliOutcome u) ...decoded))
   184	                    (1 : Op (ιB' × PauliRegister P))
   185	                  - pauliProjOnA'' P W u).mulVec (idealState P aux)‖ ^ 2)
   186	                ≤ deltaQld a b ε P.m P.d P.q ∧
   187	              (symmetric B-side bound)
   188	```

   190	Supporting definitions in Soundness.lean (all NEW, Lean-only):
   191	`idealState P aux := reindexState prodShuffle (vecTensor aux (eprState (PauliRegister P)))`;
   192	`pauliQuestion P W : (pauliBasisTest P).QuestionA := (PauliType.pauli W, 0)` (the
   193	`(Pauli, W)` question has content `0`, image of the 0-level CL function);
   194	`pauliProjOnA'' P W u : Op ((ιA' × Reg) × (ιB' × Reg))` places `pauliProj W u` on the
   195	`A''` factor, identity elsewhere (and the `B''` analogue). The A-side measurement
   196	outcome family is the sub-family of `S.A` at outcomes `PauliAnswer.pauliOutcome u`
   197	(other constructors carry no mass in the ideal comparison; define the family by
   198	pattern-matching `PauliAnswer → Op` with `0` on the other constructors — this is the
   199	faithful reading of "answer summation over `u ∈ F_q^M`").

   201	## (e) Settled encoding decisions (do not re-derive)
   202	
   203	1. **Polynomials — representative convention** (issue #0004, `def:polynomials-degree`):
   204	   polynomial-valued objects are representatives, not function classes. Reuse
   205	   `MIPStarRE.LDT.Preliminaries.polyFunc` where a polynomial *class* is quantified.
   206	   Game *answers* are finite coefficient tuples exactly as printed in the paper
   207	   ("given by its d+1 coefficients"): `Fin (d+1) → K`, resp. `Fin (m*d+1) → K`.
   208	   Do not reuse `LDT.AxisLinePolynomial`/`DiagonalLineAnswer` (the LDT diagonal answer
   209	   is function-encoded and `Parameters`-bundled; a bridge can come later).
   210	   `def:ld-meas`/`PolyMeas` are NOT in this closure — do not build them now.
   211	2. **Distributions — match LDT, not PMF**: the LDT question distributions use
   212	   `MIPStarRE.LDT.Distribution` (Finset-supported, real weights, `Error := ℝ`) with
   213	   `IsProbability`, `avgOver`, `map`, `uniformDistribution`, `uniformOnFinset`
   214	   (`LDT/Basic/Distribution.lean`, `DistributionUniform.lean`; product combinators in
   215	   `DistributionProduct.lean` — verify the exact name before use). All QPBT question
   216	   distributions are `Distribution` values; `PMF` only ever via the existing
   217	   `DistributionPMF` bridge, never in game-facing statements.
   218	3. **Measurements**: use `MIPStarRE.Quantum.Measurement`/`Submeasurement`
   219	   (`Quantum/Measurement.lean`) as the POVM carrier; marginals and the bracket
   220	   notation are `Measurement.postprocess` (already `\leanok` for ch12 `def:bracket`).
   221	   Projectivity via `MIPStarRE.Quantum.IsProj`.
   222	4. **States**: pure states as unit vectors of `EuclideanSpace ℂ ι` (the theorem's
   223	   conclusion needs vector norms, isometries `→ₗᵢ[ℂ]` — reuse
   224	   `Quantum/FiniteHilbert.lean` patterns — and `eprState`). The density-matrix
   225	   `LDT.QuantumState` layer is NOT used in the QPBT games layer.
   226	5. **Field model**: reuse `MIPStarRE.LDT.FieldModel q` (bundled `K ≃ Fin q`). The χ
   227	   map (eq:chi-func) interprets `s : K` as an integer through `FieldModel.equiv`;
   228	   the finite-field trace is the basis-independent `Algebra.trace (ZMod 2) K`
   229	   (= Tr of `Algebra.leftMulMatrix`, i.e. eq:def-trace). The self-dual normal basis
   230	   and `def:binary-representation` are NOT in the statement closure and are deferred
   231	   (see OPEN-6). `canonicalComplement` is defined basis-freely by the pivot
   232	   characterization — `j` is a pivot of `W` iff restricting to coordinates `≤ j`
   233	   increases rank — which agrees with the source's RREF construction by the
   234	   basis-independence noted in `def:canonical-complement` (equivalence proof deferred).
   235	6. **Qudit indexing**: the `M = 2^m` qudits and the vectors `F_q^M` are indexed by
   236	   `Cube m := Fin m → Bool`. Never introduce `Fin (2^m)`; `M` appears only as
   237	   `Fintype.card (Cube m)` in docstrings.
   238	7. **Prose claims inside blueprint definitions become companion lemmas**: CL-level
   239	   assertions ("`L_ALine` is a 2-level CL function"), uniformity of `χ(s)`,
   240	   well-definedness remarks — each a named `sorry` lemma next to the definition, not
   241	   a definitional obligation. Definitions themselves are direct and computable-shaped.
   242	8. **Asymptotic `≈`/O(·) → quantitative functionals**: `def:state-distance` /
   243	   `def:povm-distance` are encoded as explicit real error quantities (`stateDistSq`,
   244	   `opFamilyDistSq`), mirroring how the LDT track already quantifies `≃`/`≈`
   245	   (cf. rem:asymptotic-distance). The implicit universal constants of the blueprint's
   246	   `≈_δ` are absorbed into the existentially quantified constant `a` of
   247	   `pauli_soundness`; record this in the theorem docstring.
   248	9. **Win predicates are `Bool`-valued**, answer alphabets are sum types, and
   249	   "answers not of the prescribed form are rejected" is a predicate clause (match on
   250	   constructor shape). Question alphabets are `Type × ambient-space` pairs — contents
   251	   are full ambient vectors `ι → K` (images of the CL maps), not per-type refined
   252	   types; this matches the blueprint's `(t, L_t(z))` format.
   253	10. **`deltaQld` argument order** is `(ε, m, d, q)` with `0 < b < 1` strict and
   254	    prefactor `a(md)^a` — per rem:delta-qld-argument-order; do not copy the classical
   255	    `δ_ld` shape.

   154	/-- Soundness function of the Pauli basis test; argument order (ε, m, d, q)
   155	everywhere, per rem:delta-qld-argument-order. Real rpow throughout. -/

open Matrix

variable {m n : Type*}

namespace Matrix

variable [Fintype n] [DecidableEq n]

/-- A shorthand for `Matrix.toLpLin 2 2`. -/
abbrev toEuclideanLin : Matrix m n 𝕜 ≃ₗ[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n →ₗ[𝕜] EuclideanSpace 𝕜 m :=
  toLpLin 2 2

@[deprecated toLpLin_toLp (since := "2026-01-22")]
lemma toEuclideanLin_toLp (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (x : n → 𝕜) :
    Matrix.toEuclideanLin A (toLp _ x) = toLp _ (Matrix.toLin' A x) := rfl

@[deprecated ofLp_toLpLin (since := "2026-01-22")]
theorem piLp_ofLp_toEuclideanLin (A : Matrix m n 𝕜) (x : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n) :
    ofLp (Matrix.toEuclideanLin A x) = Matrix.toLin' A (ofLp x) :=
  rfl

@[deprecated toLpLin_apply (since := "2026-01-22")]
theorem toEuclideanLin_apply (M : Matrix m n 𝕜) (v : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n) :
    toEuclideanLin M v = toLp _ (M *ᵥ ofLp v) := rfl

@[deprecated ofLp_toLpLin (since := "2026-01-22")]
theorem ofLp_toEuclideanLin_apply (M : Matrix m n 𝕜) (v : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 n) :
    ofLp (toEuclideanLin M v) = M *ᵥ ofLp v :=
  rfl

     7	/-!
     8	# The low-degree game
     9	
    10	This file introduces the finite question and answer alphabets used by the
    11	low-degree component of the Pauli basis test.  The maps are explicit maps on
    12	the ambient coefficient space; their conditional-linearity and distribution
    13	invariants are recorded as proof-level obligations for later stages.
    14	
    15	## References
    16	
    17	The source-facing nodes are `def:ld-game`, `def:ld-question-distribution`, and
    18	`def:ld-win-predicate` in
    19	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`; their paper origin is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-1010`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	/-- Parameters for the low-degree game, including the fixed field model used by
    30	the ambient coefficient space.  This is the Lean carrier for `def:ld-game` in
    31	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-105`, with paper origin
    32	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-1010`.
    33	-/
    34	structure LdParams where
    35	  q : ℕ
    36	  m : ℕ
    37	  d : ℕ
    38	  k : ℕ
    39	  hm : 1 ≤ m
    40	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    41	  hk : 1 ≤ k
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	  model : FixedFieldModel q
    45	
    46	/-- The scalar carrier selected by an `LdParams` record; this is the fixed
    47	field carrier in `def:ld-game`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper
    48	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    49	-/
    50	abbrev ScalarQ (P : LdParams) := P.model.K
    51	
    52	/-- The three low-degree question types of `def:ld-game`, blueprint
    53	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`, paper origin
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    55	-/
    56	inductive LdType where
    57	  | point
    58	  | aline
    59	  | dline
    60	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    61	
    62	/-- The register index used by the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    63	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    64	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`).
    65	-/
    66	abbrev LdIndex (P : LdParams) := (Fin P.m ⊕ Unit) ⊕ Fin P.m
    67	
    68	/-- The full ambient low-degree coefficient space (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
    69	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
    70	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`).
    71	-/
    72	abbrev LdSpace (P : LdParams) := LdIndex P → ScalarQ P
    73	
    74	/-- The point coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    75	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
    76	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
    77	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
    78	-/
    79	def LdSpace.point (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    80	  fun i => z (.inl (.inl i))
    81	
    82	/-- The shared scalar coordinate of an ambient low-degree vector in
    83	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
    84	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
    85	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
    86	-/
    87	def LdSpace.seed (z : LdSpace P) : ScalarQ P :=
    88	  z (.inl (.inr ()) )
    89	
    90	/-- The direction coordinates of an ambient low-degree vector in
    91	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
    92	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
    93	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
    94	-/
    95	def LdSpace.direction (z : LdSpace P) : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
    96	  fun i => z (.inr i)
    97	
    98	/-- The integer-coordinate map `χ` from the fixed field representation.  This
    99	is `eq:chi-func` in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   100	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   101	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
   102	-/
   103	noncomputable def chiIndex (P : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ P) : Fin P.m := by
   104	  letI : NeZero P.m := ⟨by
   105	    exact Nat.ne_of_gt (lt_of_lt_of_le Nat.zero_lt_one P.hm)⟩
   106	  exact Fin.ofNat P.m ((binaryRepresentation P.model s).val / (P.q / P.m))
   107	
   108	/-- The source uses the block quotient of the fixed integer representation.  The
   109	`Fin.ofNat` wrapper supplies the totalized boundary behavior for the temporary
   110	 skeleton's proof-irrelevant zero-dimension branch.  This is the projection
   111	 clause of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   112	 `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   113	 `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
   114	-/
   115	def prefixProjection (i : Fin P.m) (v : Fin P.m → ScalarQ P) :
   116	    Fin P.m → ScalarQ P :=
   117	  fun j => if j.val < i.val then 0 else v j
   118	
   119	/-- The point CL map, retaining the point block and clearing the auxiliary
   120	blocks.  It is the map `L_point` of `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   121	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   122	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
   123	-/
   124	def ldPointCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   125	  fun i => match i with
   126	  | .inl (.inl j) => z (.inl (.inl j))
   127	  | .inl (.inr _) => 0
   128	  | .inr _ => 0
   129	
   130	/-- The affine-line CL map.  The direction block is put through the canonical
   131	line representative map from `def:line-representative`, while the point block
   132	is retained (blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   133	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`).
   134	-/
   135	noncomputable def ldALineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   136	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   137	  let rep := lineRepMap (coordinateDirection i)
   138	  fun i => match i with
   139	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   140	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   141	  | .inr _ => 0
   142	
   143	/-- The diagonal-line CL map, using the same canonical representative interface
   144	for the direction block.  This is the `L_DLine` clause of
   145	`def:ld-question-distribution` (blueprint
   146	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper origin
   147	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`).
   148	-/
   149	noncomputable def ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) (z : LdSpace P) : LdSpace P :=
   150	  let i := chiIndex P (z.seed)
   151	  let direction := prefixProjection i (z.direction)
   152	  let rep := lineRepMap direction
   153	  fun i => match i with
   154	  | .inl (.inl j) => (rep (z.point)) j
   155	  | .inl (.inr _) => z (.inl (.inr ()))
   156	  | .inr j => direction j
   157	
   158	/-- Dispatch the three low-degree CL maps by question type.  This is the typed
   159	construction in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   160	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   161	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
   162	-/
   163	noncomputable def ldCL (P : LdParams) : LdType → LdSpace P → LdSpace P
   164	  | .point => ldPointCL P
   165	  | .aline => ldALineCL P
   166	  | .dline => ldDLineCL P

   173	theorem isCondLinear_ldALineCL (P : LdParams) :
   174	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 2 (ldALineCL P) := by
   175	  sorry

   178	level-3 assertion in `def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   179	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin

   182	theorem isCondLinear_ldDLineCL (P : LdParams) :
   183	    IsCondLinearOn (ScalarQ P) Finset.univ 3 (ldDLineCL P) := by
   184	  sorry
   185	
   186	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   187	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-31`; paper origin
   188	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`).
   189	-/
   190	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   191	
   192	/-- The finite edge set for the low-degree question graph.  Self-loops are
   193	included so that every type has a valid endpoint pair; this is the graph in
   194	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   195	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   196	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
   197	-/
   198	def ldEdges : Finset (Sym2 LdType) :=
   199	  (Finset.univ.image (fun t : LdType => Sym2.mk t t)) ∪
   200	    ({Sym2.mk .point .aline, Sym2.mk .point .dline} : Finset (Sym2 LdType))
   201	
   202	/-- The support of the typed CL question distribution, obtained by pushing a
   203	uniform seed through the type-indexed maps.  This is the construction in
   204	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint
   205	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`, paper origin
   206	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
   207	-/
   208	noncomputable def ldQuestionSupport (P : LdParams) :
   209	    Finset (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   210	  (Finset.univ : Finset ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P)).image (fun s =>
   211	    ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   212	
   213	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   214	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:38-49`; paper
   215	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:979-1009`.
   216	-/
   217	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   218	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
